objective: Production-ready English-first Sahih al-Bukhari reader with the full collection, precise source access, Cedar narration, whole-hadith sessions and dependable offline iPhone use.

decisions.search: Exact words/phrases and reference numbers first; no semantic topics or inferred summaries.
decisions.personalData: Downloadable local backup first. No accounts or cross-device server needed.
decisions.content: Keep raw Arabic, published translation, narration script and generated speech as separately versioned artifacts. Translation and audio approvals must identify the exact text hashes reviewed.
decisions.numbering: Namespace source IDs and edition references. Never assume one edition's book or hadith number equals another's.
decisions.architecture: Keep the static PWA. Split collection metadata, book text packs, search index and audio packs; load text and download audio independently. Preserve the persistent media element and waiting-worker update behavior.
decisions.publication: Candidate import is not reader approval. Resolve source coverage and rights, then review complete narrator chains, narration, chapter context and any source notes separately. Preserve repeated narrations; do not deduplicate by meaning.

requirements.remaining: Resolve 173 absent numbered records and 10 empty numbered records in the first candidate; compare another edition and printed witness; preserve chapter material and variant references. A second edition has numeric markers 1–7124 but includes mislabeled chapter headings, suffixed records and a duplicate 3905; it needs its own inventory and reference map.

sourceResearch.finding: The source explains numbering differences and restricts scraping and mass reproduction, directing snapshot requests to its API. Do not bulk copy the website.
Translations may be redistributed unchanged with attribution, version information and update conditions. This is a selected hadith encyclopedia, not demonstrated complete ordered Bukhari coverage.
The intentions entry includes a Muslim reference and an alternate Bukhari wording; it cannot be substituted for the exact opening Bukhari record or its full chain.
OpenITI permits noncommercial share-alike reuse with attribution and warns that text fidelity varies. Its source ID and Git commit are pinned in the local candidate manifest.
The linked top-level index lists 73 sections. This is insufficient evidence of full-collection coverage or equivalence to a 97-book numbering scheme.
